name: Lina Carbone
life: “I still remember hearing a familiar voice after half a lifetime.” Sunday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Lina can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I was the last person she called. The message was about soup, and its ordinariness is why I kept it.
appearance: Lina has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Lina draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Lina takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To preserve the last ordinary phone message.
family: Camille Breen is Lina’s younger cousin. Lina brings a spare shopping bag. Camille chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The return of a witness*, Camille says, “I was jailed for something else and shared a cell with the man she named.”
connections: Linden Owen. The worker waiting for renewal learns that the last call was ordinary and probably precious.
